request.contents:
Is this clause enforceable in a residential lease in Ontario? Cite the section.

Read the clause as a term of an ordinary private residential tenancy in Ontario that the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 covers: the rental unit has no exemption under section 6.1, and it is not student housing, a care home, a co-operative or a mobile home park.

Clause: Pets are welcome. The Tenant shall pay a refundable pet deposit of $250, which will be returned at the end of the tenancy if there is no pet damage.

End your answer with these two lines:
Verdict: enforceable (or: Verdict: not enforceable)
Section: <the number of the one section of the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 that decides it>

text:
In Ontario, a landlord is strictly prohibited from requiring or receiving any security deposit other than a rent deposit (commonly known as the last month's rent deposit). Because the $250 pet deposit is a security deposit for potential damage rather than a lawful rent deposit, this clause contravenes Section 105 of the *Residential Tenancies Act, 2006* (and is consequently void under Section 4).

Verdict: not enforceable
Section: 105
